scope: Actual armoured standoff caller connected to selected-platform native movement/retirement, replacing group waypoint
implementation: CortexVehicles retains the existing known-AT/fully-mounted/contact trigger and screened single-leg destination choice. It starts the operation with only the selected original operating actors, captures a single60-second expiry and admits VehicleTacticalMoveStart after exact owner/epoch/operation/lease/crew/native-baseline checks. No group waypoint or group split.

One finite vehicleTacticalMove FSM uses shared VehicleCrewMoveNativePhase. Exact current worker/token/serial/epoch/reference and original route/crew/control checks fence native writes. Measured progress/rest permits HOLD; original expiry/feature or operation loss requests bounded handback. Native acknowledgement is separate from physical arrival.

Original-actor casualty retirement follows the existing original-survivor policy. New owner/dead worker maintenance uses shared VehicleCrewMoveRetire for retirement only, preserving cleanup clocks; live current workers remain alone.

CortexOwnershipLease and DrivingMovementAvailable refuse new ownership while selected-native reference persists, even after ordinary expiry. CortexGroupTick and CortexVehicles retain that reservation. CortexStop requests retirement after controlled epoch change; locality/discovery service exact pending original work.

Standoff admission runs before scripted gunnery. This layer defers scripted fire for the pending original operating actors or unknown reference, preventing its own fire intents from replacing their MOVE/return acknowledgement. Other gun stations and native self-defence remain available.

Failed pre-ISSUE worker allocation retires its reference/local lease/generation without native commands. Terminal acknowledged native handback retires only matching state and operation; unresolved proof is retained, not erased to permit another controller.

bounds.cleanupSeconds: Original shared finite policy, at most holdUntil+30; no renewal on migration or repeated maintenance.
bounds.cost: One finite worker for an active selected episode; two-actor observations, existing route plan and bounded reference service. No permanent worker/world scan. Runtime cost unmeasured.

validation.focused: 610 existing tactical operation cases passed. Existing affected waypoint contracts updated to native admission/lifecycle wiring; no test count growth.
validation.development: Initial coverage attempt incorrectly included FSM in SQF-only source assignment; removed and regenerated. Initial focused tests exposed3 affected legacy waypoint assertions; updated to the current command path and retained their movement/deadline/cancellation requirements.

limits: No Arma audit was launched. Actual path following, standoff/handback success, repeated use, casualty, driver/commander planning, owner migration, intervention and5%median/10%p95 performance are unverified.

Admission retains the original fully-mounted-group trigger and refuses native commands outside idle/MOVE/WAIT, including FIRE. It does not provide arbitrary mixed foot/vehicle task admission. Native formation following is not explicitly controlled.
Chosen destination is screened; actual native path may deviate and requires physical verification.

Unresolved native orders, deleted platforms, changed original seats or unsuccessful expired cleanup remain reserved; a proven supersession/deleted-platform recovery path is still required for robust general availability. No terminal claim from elapsed time or a dead script.
This implements selected standoff, not post-shot cover relocation, actual-shot manoeuvre triggers, whole Protocol/LAMBS/HBQ parity or behavioural acceptance.
